gloss: to wake up; to awaken; to come to one's senses

definitions.explanation: To transition from sleep to a waking state. An intransitive expression describing the natural process of waking up, as opposed to being woken by someone else.

definitions.gloss: to come to one's senses; to have one's eyes opened
definitions.explanation: To suddenly realize the truth of a situation, snap out of a delusion, or become aware of something one was previously blind to. Used figuratively for moments of realization or disillusionment.

examples.english: I woke up at 6 in the morning.

examples.japanese: ⟦{物音|ものおと}→物音：03633_monooto⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{目|め}が{覚|さ}めてしまった。
examples.english: I was woken up by a noise.

examples.japanese: ⟦{夜中|よなか}→夜中：01008_yonaka⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{何度|なんど}→何度：17592_nando⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧{目|め}が{覚|さ}めて、⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦{眠|ねむ}れなかった→眠れる：15166_nemureru⟧。
examples.english: I woke up many times during the night and couldn't sleep well.

examples.japanese: ⟦あの→あの：00915_ano⟧⟦{失敗|しっぱい}→失敗：01636_shippai⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{目|め}が{覚|さ}めた。
⟦{友人|ゆうじん}→友人：03649_yuujin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{一言|ひとこと}→一言：03708_hitokoto⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{目|め}が{覚|さ}める⟦{思|おも}い→思い：10248_omoi⟧だった。
examples.english: My friend's single remark was a real wake-up call.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧ようやく{目|め}が{覚|さ}めて、⟦{自分|じぶん}→自分：02887_jibun⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{間違|まちが}い→間違い：03733_machigai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{気|き}づいた。
examples.english: He finally came to his senses and realized his mistake.

notes:
An idiomatic expression built from ⟦{目|め}→目：00525_me⟧ (eye) + ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ (subject marker) + ⟦{覚|さ}める→覚める：02058_sameru⟧ (to awaken, to become alert). The verb ⟦{覚|さ}める→覚める：02058_sameru⟧ is ichidan and intransitive — it describes a spontaneous change of state.

Sense 1 is the everyday meaning and one of the most common ways to say "to wake up" in Japanese. It focuses on the moment of awakening (eyes opening) rather than the act of getting out of bed.

Sense 2 extends the metaphor: just as physical eyes open from sleep, mental "eyes" open to reality. Often used when someone has been deceived, deluded, or obsessed, and finally sees things clearly.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{朝|あさ}→朝：02277_asa⟧{目|め}が{覚|さ}める: to wake up in the morning
- ⟦{夜中|よなか}→夜中：01008_yonaka⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{目|め}が{覚|さ}める: to wake up in the middle of the night
- {目|め}が{覚|さ}める⟦{思|おも}い→思い：10248_omoi⟧: a feeling of having one's eyes opened; an eye-opening experience
- {目|め}が{覚|さ}めるような: eye-opening; strikingly vivid (e.g., of a color)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{起|お}きる→起きる：00521_okiru⟧: to get up — covers both waking and getting out of bed; more general
- ⟦{目|め}を{覚|さ}ます→目を覚ます：26079_mewosamasu⟧: to wake up (transitive/volitional) — an active choice to wake, vs. the spontaneous {目|め}が{覚|さ}める
- ⟦{目覚|めざ}める→目覚める：04649_mezameru⟧: to awaken — a single-word literary synonym, also used figuratively for awakening to a new awareness or ability
